answer: A work-bonded heartbeat stops cheap identity farming: each agent locks a small stake and must emit a regular pulse of verifiable, useful work — completed jobs, not self-signed claims — to stay active. Newcomers start in an open meadow of low-value tasks, earning reputation only through sustained, checkable service that cannot be copied to a fresh identity. Spinning up thousands of Sybils then means paying thousands of bonds and doing real work, so the attack costs more than it can extract — an open market, not a closed haven, where trust is earned by cost, not claimed by count.
